correctness.rationale: Multiplicativity reduces the problem to a strictly monotone product of four rational factors. Exact inequalities force four ordered first-two-prime possibilities and finite third-prime upper bounds. Necessary inequalities restrict these to twelve prime triples; the equation uniquely determines the fourth prime and exact primality tests yield precisely eight cases. Each solution directly verifies the original identity; no unverified infinite exhaustion is inferred from finite trials. A standard-library verifier reproduces every critical finite step.

evidence: Broughan–Delbourgo (JIS 16, 13.8.8) classify at most three distinct prime factors and prove more general finiteness bounds.
Broughan–Zhou (JIS 17, 14.9.2), in its inspected theorems and tables, addresses small prime support and gives 24871 as a four-prime example.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general finiteness upper bound does not imply an eight-element exact classification, and low-support theorems do not contain the four-prime case. Conversely, a single example or numerical list is not proof of exhaustion.

evidence: For squarefree integers, Dedekind psi(n)=sigma(n), so psi(n)=2phi(n) is literally equivalent on this domain.
OEIS A292390 records an equivalent ratio problem but no proof of the all-four-prime exhaustion in its inspected record.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Algebraic equivalence means non-identical function names cannot justify originality. The specific all-four-prime theorem was not found under the equivalent psi terminology; this is limited evidence, not a uniqueness proof.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: This is substantial exact prior tabulation of all result values; the new claim is not that those values were unknown, but that the four-prime squarefree fiber has no other values anywhere. The inspected tables alone provide no such global proof.

originality.rationale: The numbers appear in OEIS A062699, so novelty is exclusively the unrestricted exhaustive classification for squarefree integers with exactly four distinct prime factors. Broughan–Delbourgo (2013) prove the three-prime boundary and general finite bounds, while Broughan–Zhou (2014) display one four-prime example but do not give the exact four-prime classification in the inspected material. No exact theorem recovered through equivalent psi formulation, indexed searches, or accessible historical claims. Residual priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Historical priority: another unindexed proof might enumerate the complete squarefree four-prime layer.
A sequence records every one of the eight integers, so only proof of unbounded completeness is original; novel terms are not claimed.

value.rationale: The first squarefree prime-support stratum beyond the published complete at-most-three classification is a motivated natural Diophantine classification. The eight integer values were known as sequence terms, but the proof determines the exact complete stratum at all sizes and illustrates a transferable monotone rational-product bound. This is stronger than table recomputation, while deliberately excluding nonsquarefree cases.
